title: Customer threads concordance and low-risk probe catalog
summary: Compact working notebook that aligns overlapping customer threads into candidate low-effort probes and a prioritized micro-catalog for next three sprints. Focus is on actionable small fixes, mitigation playbooks, and minimal-risk UX experiments that reduce friction for Dedicated and Hosted API users.
body:
Context:
- Pulled ~120 raw tickets + transcripts (April-Nov 2026) across support, AE notes, and field interviews. This doc stitches recurring friction signals into concordant threads and proposes low-risk probes (MVP changes, feature flags, UX copy/flows, server-side defaults).

Highlights observed (themes):
1) Latency shock on cold-starts for short-burst workloads:
   - Multiple SMBs report 2x latency when model swapped/fallback triggered 
   - Root hints: routing to compatible variant with different kv-cache layout; missing warm-up calls on client flows
   - Customer cost sensitivity: prefer small latency fixes (caching heuristics) vs larger infra commits

2) Token-cost surprises for multi-step evals:
   - Users surprised by reranking+embedding combos, not obvious from console pricing page
   - Confusion about how batching affects per-token billing for mixed-size requests

3) Private deployment onboarding friction:
   - Docs gap on KMS integration examples for common enterprise KMS providers
 - Networking checklist ambiguous (subnet config + NAT egress)

4) Observability blindspots at route-level:
   - Teams want token-level cost traces tied to deployment variant (dedicated vs hosted)
   - Tracing for fallback model invocations is incomplete in current console traces

Concordant thread samples (short):
- Thread A: "unexpected latency spike when fallback to smaller model occurs" (3 customers, Feb-Jun 2026)
- Thread B: "billing jump when enabling rerank after embedding call" (2 mid-market customers)
- Thread C: "deploy on-prem: KMS error unclear, install loop during preflight" (5 customers across two sectors)

Low-risk probe catalog (ranked by expected impact / low implementation risk):
A. Server-side warm-up hints (probing):
   - What: Add an opt-in route-level warm-up flag that triggers a short prefix request to populate KV cache after a fallback or model swap.
   - Why: Addresses cold-start latency for short-burst apps without infra changes.
   - Acceptance: 10–50ms median improvement in synthetic short-burst bench for canary customers.
   - Downside: small extra tokens consumed; expose opt-out.

B. Pricing micro-copy and in-console calculator tweak:
   - What: Inline examples for common flows (rerank after embed, chat + tool-call) and a calculator toggle for batching assumptions.
   - Why: Reduces token-cost surprises; low dev cost (docs + console small UI)
   - Acceptance: Customer-reported clarity metric + drop in billing follow-up threads by 30% for trial cohort.

C. KMS quickstart templates and preflight checklist (docs + script):
   - What: Add provider-specific examples (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, HashiCorp) and a preflight script that validates network/KMS roles.
   - Why: Removes friction for Private onboarding; reduces L3 handoffs
   - Acceptance: Decrease in onboarding time & reduced repeated field calls

D. Route-level fallback tracing flag (observability):
   - What: Add an opt-in trace tag that logs model fallback decision and cost delta per request in Console traces.
   - Why: Faster root-cause for performance regressions and billing surprises
   - Acceptance: Faster RCA time in SRE/Support tickets, plus improved confidence for customers running hybrid routing policies

Unresolved questions / open assumptions:
- Will customers accept token-cost overhead for server-side warm-up? (assume opt-in by default)
- How to model expected cost delta for warm-up across different customer traffic patterns? Need simple heuristic in docs/console.
- KMS script scope: run locally vs run as part of Private installer? (Ops preference leans to preflight local script)

Quick pilot plan (6 weeks):
- Week 0: pick 3 pilot customers (1 SMB hosted, 1 mid-market dedicated, 1 enterprise private) — request opt-in for warm-up and fallback traces. (Owner: Miguel)
- Week 1–2: implement console copy + calculator tweak; land docs KMS quickstarts (Owner: Eleni)
- Week 3: release warm-up flag behind feature gate to canary infra + add trace opt-in (Owner: Serving Runtime + Observability leads)
- Week 4–5: monitor telemetry (latency percentiles, token delta), gather qualitative feedback (customer interviews)
- Week 6: sync CS + Product on go/no-go and follow-up backlog items

Action items (immediate):
- [ ] Miguel: draft pilot outreach note + onboard pilot customers (due 2026-11-20)
- [ ] Eleni: PR for console help copy and calculator wire (due 2026-11-24)
- [ ] Samir: scope warm-up implementation with serving-runtime, surface resource/token accounting (due 2026-11-23)
- [ ] Priya: create Confluence page with aggregated transcripts and attach JIRA-CS-798 (done)

Notes to self / friction snippets (raw):
- "We moved to dedicated and the spikes went away — but new bill came — what's the delta?" — AE note, May 2026
- "Preflight error: 403 KMS key not found — logs show only generic 500" — field note, Aug 2026
- Quick check: console telemetry for fallback count by route exists but not correlated to token cost (easy join missing)

Proposed next discussion agenda (CS <> Product <> Serving Runtime):
1) Validate prioritization: warm-up vs routing heuristics (size vs frequency tradeoffs)
2) Constrain simplest warm-up implementation that keeps token overhead explicit and reversible
3) Decide owner and SLAs for KMS preflight script and docs
